timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg pv profile
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative PV output, kW per kW installed, one value per hour of the day (about 5 kWh per kWp per day). Replace it with your own measured or modelled profile.

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg load profile
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative household demand, normalised to its evening peak, one value per hour of the day (about 9 times the peak in kWh per day).

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg tariff
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative time-of-use import price, EUR/kWh, by hour of the day.

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg flat tariff
timeseries_inputs.description: A flat import price, EUR/kWh: one value, held for the whole run.

timeseries_inputs.name: Nrg grid intensity
timeseries_inputs.description: Illustrative grid carbon intensity, kg CO2e per kWh, by hour of the day: cleaner around midday, dirtier at the evening peak.

levels.name: Nrg Battery
levels.description: Energy stored, kWh. The bounds are the usable state-of-charge window.

flows.name: Nrg PV
flows.description: Generation injected into the site bus, kW.

flows.name: Nrg load
flows.description: Site demand drawn from the bus, kW.

flows.name: Nrg charge
flows.description: Power drawn from the site bus to charge, kW. Saturation stops it when the battery is full, and what it could not take is spilled -- surplus for the export or curtailment accounting to pick up.
flows.rate: min(charge_kw, (dispatch == "self_consumption") * max(FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in", merit), 0) + (dispatch == "tariff_arbitrage") * (TS(price_profile) < charge_below_price) * charge_kw + (dispatch == "policy") * max(VAR("$nrg_setpoint_kw"), 0))

flows.name: Nrg discharge
flows.description: Energy taken OUT of the battery, kW: what the bus needs divided by the discharge efficiency.
flows.rate: min(discharge_kw, (dispatch == "self_consumption") * max(FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out", merit), 0) + (dispatch == "tariff_arbitrage") * (TS(price_profile) > discharge_above_price) * min(discharge_kw, max(FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_out", merit), 0)) + (dispatch == "policy") * max(-VAR("$nrg_setpoint_kw"), 0)) / discharge_efficiency

flows.name: Nrg storage output
flows.description: Power actually injected into the site bus, kW -- what the battery managed after its power limit and its state of charge, times the discharge efficiency.

flows.name: Nrg cycles
flows.description: Equivalent full cycles: energy delivered divided by the nameplate capacity. Its Total is the cycle count, for degradation and for a sustainability assessment.

flows.name: Nrg import
flows.description: Whatever the site could not cover itself, up to the connection limit, kW.
flows.rate: min(max(FLOWSUM("demand") + FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out") - FLOWSUM("dispatchable"), 0), import_limit_kw)

flows.name: Nrg unserved
flows.description: Demand the connection limit could not deliver, kW.
flows.rate: max(FLOWSUM("demand") + FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out") - FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOW("$Nrg import"), 0)

flows.name: Nrg export
flows.description: Surplus sold to the grid, up to the export limit, kW. A negative price is revenue.
flows.rate: min(max(FLOWSUM("generation") + FLOWSUM("storage_out") + FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in"), 0), export_limit_kw)

flows.name: Nrg curtailed
flows.description: Generation that was neither used, stored nor exported, kW.
flows.rate: max(FLOWSUM("generation") + FLOWSUM("storage_out") + FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOW("$Nrg export"), 0)

fixed_costs.name: Nrg PV capital
fixed_costs.description: Capital cost of the array, annualised and prorated over the run.

fixed_costs.name: Nrg battery capital
fixed_costs.description: Capital cost of the pack and its inverter, annualised and prorated over the run.

info.description: Non-dispatchable generation from a normalised profile: output = profile x installed capacity x performance ratio. The profile is one value per hour of the day, in kW per kW installed, so the same asset is a wind turbine or a run-of-river plant with a different profile. Its output joins the site bus under the tag "generation", which every dispatchable asset reads -- place two arrays with different profiles and they simply add up. The annualised capital cost is a FIXED cost, prorated over the run, so a sizing run over installed_kwp compares like with like. No ports: this is a continuous asset, nothing flows through it.

parameters.name: installed_kwp
parameters.label: Installed capacity
parameters.help: Peak DC capacity. The profile is per kW installed, so this is the multiplier.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.label: Output profile
parameters.help: Normalised output, kW per kW installed, by hour of the day. Edit the values in the model's Time series tab, or import a measured year from CSV.

parameters.name: performance_ratio
parameters.label: Performance ratio
parameters.help: Everything between the panel rating and the meter: soiling, temperature, inverter and cable losses.

parameters.name: capex_per_kwp
parameters.label: Capital cost
parameters.help: Installed cost per kWp. Charged into Total Cost as a fixed cost (see the annual cost rate), so a sizing run trades it against the energy it saves.

parameters.name: annual_cost_rate
parameters.label: Annual cost rate
parameters.help: Fraction of the capital cost charged per year -- depreciation plus cost of capital. The charge is PRORATED over the run: amount x HORIZON / 8760, so a one-week run pays one week of it and capex and operating cost cover the same window. 0 leaves the capital cost out of Total Cost entirely. The model's time unit must be hours.

info.description: Storage with power limits, separate charge and discharge efficiencies, a usable state-of-charge window and three dispatch rules. "self_consumption" charges on the site's surplus and discharges on its deficit; "tariff_arbitrage" charges whenever the price is below a threshold and discharges to cover the load when it is above another; "policy" follows this battery's OWN setpoint variable, <instance>/nrg_setpoint_kw (positive charges, negative discharges), which a Policy-mode DECIDE -- or nagasim.rl -- writes; each Battery storage instance has its own, so a site may train two. It reads the site bus (generation, demand and what storage ahead of it in the merit order already took) and injects into it, so a second battery with a higher merit number sees exactly the surplus the first one left. Equivalent full cycles are reported as a flow; the annualised capital cost is a FIXED cost, prorated over the run, so a sizing study trades it against the energy it saves. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

parameters.name: capacity_kwh
parameters.label: Nameplate capacity
parameters.help: Total energy capacity. The USABLE window is min_soc..max_soc of this. A run without storage is this asset with both power limits at 0, not a capacity of 0.

parameters.name: min_soc
parameters.label: Minimum state of charge
parameters.help: Fraction of the nameplate capacity kept in reserve; the battery never discharges below it.

parameters.name: initial_soc
parameters.label: Initial state of charge
parameters.help: Where the run starts, as a fraction of the nameplate capacity. Keep it inside the min/max window.

parameters.name: charge_kw
parameters.label: Charge power
parameters.help: Largest power drawn from the site bus while charging (before the charge efficiency).

parameters.name: discharge_kw
parameters.label: Discharge power
parameters.help: Largest power DELIVERED to the site bus while discharging (after the discharge efficiency).

parameters.name: charge_efficiency
parameters.label: Charge efficiency
parameters.help: Energy stored per unit drawn from the bus.

parameters.name: discharge_efficiency
parameters.label: Discharge efficiency
parameters.help: Energy delivered to the bus per unit taken out of the battery.

parameters.name: standby_loss_kw
parameters.label: Standby loss
parameters.help: Constant self-consumption of the battery and its electronics. Only a CONSTANT loss is modelled; a loss proportional to the state of charge would make the trajectory exponential.

parameters.name: dispatch
parameters.label: Dispatch rule
parameters.help: self_consumption: charge on the site's surplus, discharge on its deficit. tariff_arbitrage: charge whenever the price is below the low threshold, discharge to cover the load when it is above the high one. policy: follow this instance's own setpoint variable, named <instance>/nrg_setpoint_kw after the block you dropped (the "bat_1" instance reads "bat_1/nrg_setpoint_kw"), written by a Policy-mode DECIDE or by nagasim.rl.

parameters.name: initial_setpoint_kw
parameters.label: Starting setpoint
parameters.help: What this battery's own setpoint variable holds before a controller first writes it. Only "policy" dispatch reads it; 0 means the battery idles until it is told otherwise.

parameters.name: price_profile
parameters.label: Price profile
parameters.help: The price the arbitrage rule watches. Ignored by the other two rules.

parameters.name: charge_below_price
parameters.label: Charge below
parameters.help: Arbitrage: charge at full power whenever the price is strictly below this.

parameters.name: discharge_above_price
parameters.label: Discharge above
parameters.help: Arbitrage: discharge to cover the site load whenever the price is strictly above this. The battery never exports, so no energy is created when the export limit binds.

parameters.name: merit
parameters.label: Merit order
parameters.help: Dispatch order among the storage on this bus: 1 is served first, and a battery with a higher number sees only the surplus (or deficit) the ones before it left.

parameters.name: capex_per_kw
parameters.label: Capital cost per kW
parameters.help: Power-related capital cost (the inverter), charged on the discharge power.

parameters.name: annual_cost_rate
parameters.label: Annual cost rate
parameters.help: Fraction of the capital cost charged per year -- depreciation plus cost of capital. The charge is PRORATED over the run: amount x HORIZON / 8760, so a one-week run pays one week of it and capex and operating cost cover the same window. 0 leaves the capital cost out of Total Cost entirely. The model's time unit must be hours.

info.description: The meter: whatever the site cannot cover itself is imported and priced on a tariff profile, whatever it cannot use or store is exported up to the export limit, and the rest is curtailed. Import beyond the import limit is recorded as unserved demand rather than silently supplied. Emissions follow a grid intensity profile, so a sustainability assessment is the same run. Place exactly one per site: it is the slack that closes the energy balance. No ports: this is a continuous asset. A demand charge on the peak import power is billed once at the end of the run.

parameters.name: import_profile
parameters.label: Import tariff
parameters.help: Import price by hour of the day, EUR/kWh. A flat tariff is a one-value profile.

parameters.name: export_price
parameters.label: Export price
parameters.help: Paid for every exported kWh: it enters Total Cost as a negative cost.

parameters.name: intensity_profile
parameters.label: Grid carbon intensity
parameters.help: kg CO2e per imported kWh, by hour of the day. It drives Total Impact, which is deliberately generic: use it for water, waste or any other per-unit impact instead.

parameters.name: import_limit_kw
parameters.label: Import limit
parameters.help: Connection capacity. Demand beyond it is recorded as unserved energy, not supplied.

parameters.name: export_limit_kw
parameters.label: Export limit
parameters.help: Largest power the meter may export. Surplus beyond it is curtailed, which the curtailment flow accounts for.

parameters.name: demand_charge_per_kw
parameters.label: Demand charge
parameters.help: Billed once on the highest import power the site actually HELD (the import flow's Peak Rate), the way a network operator bills capacity. 0 for an energy-only tariff.

info.title: PV + battery site (library assets)
info.description: A PV + battery site built entirely from the Energy and grid library: a PV array, a household load, a battery on the self-consumption rule and a grid connection with a time-of-use tariff and a carbon-intensity profile. Nothing is wired: the four assets meet on the site BUS, the named flow tags that FLOWSUM() adds up. Base unit hours, the real week of Monday 15 June 2026 in Europe/Rome: the daily PV, load, tariff and carbon profiles repeat "daily" in calendar terms and every result axis is a date.
info.author: Naga
info.notes: Total Cost is the weekly energy bill PLUS the annualised capital cost of the PV and the battery charged over the same week, so it is the objective a sizing run minimises: naga optimize --factor blocks.<battery block>.params.arguments.capacity_kwh=continuous:0.1:30 --factor blocks.<pv block>.params.arguments.installed_kwp=continuous:0:15 --response system/Total Cost --goal min. Total Impact is kg CO2e on the grid intensity profile.
